### problem_chain

Root problem (customer's ask): pay the account off in full today and close it (user_scenario: "you want to pay off whatever is left on the financing today, in full, and have the account closed as paid off").

Walk from the payoff rule:
1. Prerequisite sentence 1 (E1): "The payoff figure is fixed only after the account carries the late fee owed for every statement period whose installment stayed unpaid past its grace period." State at 2026-10-01: the 2026-09 installment (600.48 due 2026-09-13; balance then 591.84) received only 250.00 on 2026-09-10 (`ead9b473…12a3`) and nothing since; grace (10 days, due date = day 0) ran out after 2026-09-23. No `late_fee` line for 2026-09 exists (the only late fee, `93c02c2f…c510`, is for 2025-11 and was reversed by `727e78d1…d116`). The 2025-11 installment, the only other period paid late, carries its fee. → **unmet**. The late-fee rule ("A late fee is charged for every statement period whose required payment is still unpaid more than late_fee_grace_days … posted on the first day after that period's statement closes") describes the resolving write: post the 2026-09 late fee on 2026-10-01.
2. Prerequisite sentence 2 (E2): "The payoff figure is not fixed until the account carries the post-promotional interest charge for every statement period that closed after the promotion ended." State: promo ended 2026-09-13; the 2026-09 statement closed 2026-09-30, after it; the account has no `interest` line at all. → **unmet**. The post-promo rule ("the balance left accrues post-promotional interest, posted once for each statement period as an interest charge on the first day after that period's statement closes") describes the write: post the 2026-09 post-promotional interest charge on 2026-10-01.
3. Neither the late-fee rule nor the post-promo rule carries a prerequisite sentence (`prerequisite: []`); walk ends.

Derived tree: payoff ← {late fee (value_input: raises `po_bal`), post-promo interest (value_input: raises `po_bal`, moves `po_days`)}; n = 2 prerequisite problems, 2 value_input edges ≥ max(1,1); no cycle; customer-owned write: `submit_payoff_payment_45ecd350` (owner=user). Topological orders: {late fee, interest} in either order, then payoff. Isomorphic to the declared `prerequisite` of `finance_ext_payoff_figure` (E1, E2).

Per-edge load-bearing (skip one prerequisite write, keep the other, recompute the payoff): skip late fee → 343.35 (vs 358.35); skip interest → 358.36 (vs 358.35). Both bear weight; E2 bears weight by one cent only, from rounding the posted charge — without the charge the per-diem anchor falls to "from the day after promo_end_date" (18 days) and re-accrues the same 17 days at the same rate (observation T0-O1).

Parallel edges: the late fee and the interest charge both raise the balance, but neither formula reads the other's value: the late fee reads late fees, reversals, payments, funded_date, monthly_payment and the plan agreement; the interest base excludes "every late fee … posted less than one whole month" so the fee, if already posted, is subtracted back out. Late-fee-first: fee 15.00, interest 1.43; interest-first: interest 1.43, fee 15.00; payoff 358.35 in both. One terminal state; the order between the two is free (it does, however, decide whether the interest-base factor bears weight — see factor_weight).

Tools do not judge prerequisites: `post_late_fee_ce58c754`, `post_post_promo_interest_b0f5a17d` and `submit_payoff_payment_45ecd350` bodies only find/create/update; a payoff submitted first would succeed (`_difficulty.md` § action_binding_and_uuids).

No wait: both prerequisites are agent postings dated today; the payoff is a one-time ACH the customer runs at hand-over.

User scenario: raises only the root (payoff). It mentions no late fee, no interest; "Whatever the agent says needs to be put on the account or sorted out on their side first, you simply say that is fine and to go ahead; you never suggest anything yourself" is passive and conditional on the agent. Closure: "Once the payment goes through and you hear that the account is paid off and closed, you thank the agent and end the call; you do not ask for letters, statements or anything else" — closes at the last write. No unanswered ask.

Write 2 — post-promotional interest (agent, `post_post_promo_interest_b0f5a17d`), statement_period 2026-09, 2026-10-01:

## findings

- **T0-F1 — SOURCE-FACTOR RED.**
  - Symptom: `post_promo_interest_base`, the only `method` factor of the post-promotional interest computation, does not bear weight in one of the two write orders the policy permits.
  - Root cause: the payoff rule makes the late fee and the post-promotional interest charge parallel prerequisites (E1, E2) with no edge or sentence ordering them; the interest-base ladder's tier 2 ("the most recent payment was not returned and late fees or returned-payment fees were posted less than one whole month before the date of handling") is reached only if the late fee was already posted today. In this world no other fee is less than one month old (the 2025-12-01 fees are 10 months old) and the most recent payment (2026-09-10) was not returned, so with the interest posted first the customer sits on the fall-through tier ("account_balance as it stands").
  - Evidence: rule sentence quoted above; compute `ip_base: … if ip_pay_returned else (MX(0, ip_bal - ip_fees_recent) if ip_fees_recent > 0 else MX(0, ip_bal))`; rows `finance_transactions/93c02c2f…` and `c8aa8db3…` (posted 2025-12-01), `ead9b473…` (2026-09-10 payment); GT `prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness`.
  - Demonstrated consequence: interest-first order — baseline `ip_base: ip_bal` gives 341.84 × 8.995 % × 17 / 365 = 1.43 = gold; the late fee (15.00) and the payoff (358.35) are unchanged by the order. An agent that never reads the interest-base rule and posts the interest first earns full credit for the step; the factor's weight depends on an order choice the policy leaves free, so it is not a weight-bearing factor of this task. With it struck, the computation has four parameter factors and no weight-bearing method factor.
  - Affected: `tasks/0.json` world (no current-month fee other than the one this task itself posts) and `computations[policy_id=finance_ext_post_promo_interest].factor_sensitivity[post_promo_interest_base]` (1.49 asserted against a world one legitimate order never produces); the order in `evaluation_criteria` steps 7/9 is the only thing exercising the factor.
  - Relation to previous revisions: first audit.
- Observations:
  - T0-O1 E2 bears weight by one cent only (358.36 vs 358.35): without the charge, the per-diem anchor's second tier re-accrues the same 17 days at the same rate; the difference is the rounding of the posted 1.43. Formally load-bearing; also changes the terminal state (the interest row).
  - T0-O2 user_scenario line "If the agent gives you a figure that is plainly just your $250-short installment or quotes something without cents, you ask them to give you the exact amount to the cent before you pay" lets the simulator reject one particular wrong figure. "$250-short installment" reads most naturally as the monthly installment less the 250.00 paid (350.48), but the unpaid remainder of the final installment (591.84 − 250.00) is 341.84 — exactly the opening balance, i.e. the figure an agent that skipped both prerequisites would quote. Under that second reading the simulator would push back on the balance-only answer, which is a calculation check the persona should not perform. The clause supplies no figure and the simulator's reading cannot be fixed from the text, so the consequence is not deterministic; recorded as an observation on the persona (`user_scenario`, third paragraph).
  - T0-O3 "still unpaid" for a partially paid installment (250.00 of 591.84) is read as unpaid; the alternative ("nothing paid") would drop the late fee and is not a defensible reading of "the required payment is still unpaid".
  - T0-O4 seeded 2025-12-04 payment labelled "make-up payment" in the rationale does not equal the make-up rule's figure for that date (see above); history only.
  - T0-O5 rationale's "multi-source" claim for the member relief does not hold in the audit's sense; requirement met by other factors.
  - Charter-global observations O-1 … O-4 checked on this world with no consequence (see policy_self_consistency).
